newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Shares return to Belgrade bourse.
newsitem.headline: Shares return to Belgrade bourse.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) traded shares on Friday for the first time in nearly a year as three Yugoslav banks listed and began selling their stock, the bourse said.
Kulska Banka, AIK banka and Panonska banka listed a total of 29.5 million dinars ($5.42 million) in ordinary shares, the report said.
* Kulska banka listed and sold five million dinars worth of shares. Each share has 10,000 dinars face value.
Shares were part of the bank's sixth issue totalling 15 million dinars and representing 13.6 percent of its founding capital.

*AIK banka Nis listed and sold 20.5 million dinars in shares. This was little over half of its 40 million dinars issue, which represented 19.6 percent of the bank's founding capital. Face value of each share is 10,000 dinars.
*Panonska banka listed four million dinars in shares out of 10 million dinars issued, but sold none. The face value is 500 dinars.
There was no one immediately available for comment on BSE.

The BSE, which also makes markets in commodities and financial instruments, has not traded equities since early 1996. The only two shares listed and traded in 1995 were those of Investbanka and Sintelon. Both were delisted late in 1996 after several months of non-trading.
